newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Martinair may have 2nd delay on China route.
newsitem.headline: Martinair may have 2nd delay on China route.

text.p: Martinair's inaugural flight from Amsterdam to China may be postponed for a second time.
The Dutch cargo and charter airline, had originally hoped to launch the new Guangzhou service on October one. Administrative problems were blamed when the service did not start on time.
A Martinair spokesman later said that the airline was then aiming for the beginning of November.
However, the airline still has not got the green light from the bankers involved.
The spokesman refused to give a new date for the twice-weekly service and added that the airline still did not know whether it will be able to launch the service in November as planned.
"We do not want to hurry, it is a new service and a new country for Martinair," he said.

He denied that Martinair, which is 50 percent owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines AV, and its Chinese partner, China Southern Airlines, had had a disagreement. But he added that a decision is still pending on the cargo space allocations.

China Southern Airlines will be opening an office at Schiphol Amsterdam airport on November one. The carrier is expected to start twice-weekly flights on the Amsterdam-China route on November 26 with either a Boeing 777 or a B767. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
